subject: NovaCorp — preflight capacity gap worksheet
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@novacorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@novacorp.com, ops-eng@novacorp.com
Date: Tue, 04 Jun 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — preliminary traffic snapshot

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the intro earlier this month. Per our call, the platform team asked me to send a short summary of our expected traffic so Redwood can validate sizing assumptions before we get to legal. High level: we plan to move two primary workloads to dedicated capacity in Q4.

Quick numbers:
- Peak QPS (per company peak event): ~280–320 requests/sec; sustained business-hour baseline ~60–90 rps.
- Average prompt length: 120 tokens; average response length: 420 tokens (generative assistant + follow-ups).
- Token mix: ~70% short conversational prompts, 30% long-form summarization.
- Typical session pattern: single-shot queries for customers, but an internal agent workload opens KV-backed sessions (avg session length 1.5 minutes, p95 45s).
- Latency target: p95 generation + network <= 250ms.

We run a multi-tenant product (web + mobile) with periodic marketing spikes (one-off blasts where QPS can double for short windows). For now we are avoiding long-lived streaming sessions.

Two asks: 1) can you send a pre-sales sizing worksheet we can fill (token distribution + concurrency buckets)? 2) do you have any redline items in your standard Dedicated contract around telemetry retention or KV cache behavior we should expect?

I'll attach a small telemetry dump from last week's pilot (sanitized). If you need anything else from infra (trace IDs, sample request/response), tell me what shape you prefer.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Director, Platform Engineering
NovaCorp

Attachment: novacorp_telemetry_sample.csv (CSV, 28KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@novacorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, contracts@novacorp.com
Date: Wed, 05 Jun 2028 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — preliminary traffic snapshot

Elena — thanks for the summary and the sample telemetry, that helps a lot.

I've attached our preflight capacity worksheet (redwood_preflight_capacity_form.xlsx) — it has token buckets, session shape questions, and an example concurrency breakdown we use to propose Dedicated SKUs. A couple of quick clarifying questions before your infra team fills it out:

- The 280–320 QPS peak: is that global or a single-region peak? If global, what fraction do you expect to route to US vs EU?
- Do any requests use streaming (server-sent partial tokens) today? You noted you’re avoiding it but wanted to confirm.
- For the KV-backed sessions, are you using per-user pinned sessions (affinity) or ephemeral session spawning? This changes how we size GPU memory and KV cache.

Initial sizing guidance (very rough):
- For your mix (13B-style open models or equivalent) with 120/420 tokens prompt/response, rough committed pool starting point: 8–12 A100-equivalent GPUs (or 10–14 L4S-class if you prefer cheaper quantized path) with autoscale headroom for short 2x spikes.
- We recommend enabling prefix KV caching for the agent workload to drop effective per-request compute by ~22–30% (measured on similar workloads).

I'll loop Marissa from infra for specific GPU-mix recommendations and to sketch a mutual action plan (MAM) and timing for a pilot.

Quick next steps:
1) Fill the worksheet and return it.
2) Marissa and I will review and send a short proposed SKU map + cost envelope.
3) We schedule a 30–45m technical walkthrough — recommend including your infra and product leads.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_preflight_capacity_form.xlsx (Excel, 36KB)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@novacorp.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@novacorp.com
Date: Thu, 06 Jun 2028 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — preliminary traffic snapshot

Elena — quick infra note from our side after skimming the sample: helpful payloads, thanks. A few practical sizing clarifications that will materially change GPU count:

- Model family: do you intend to serve a 7B/13B/70B family? The difference in memory and qkv footprint means our recommendation swings. If you plan to start with a 13B-ish variant but may switch to 70B for advanced features, let us know — we can propose a hybrid layout (a few large nodes + many smaller ones).
- Burst duration: short bursts (<60s) are friendly to autoscaling; sustained 10m+ bursts require higher committed capacity to avoid cold starts. Please indicate how long your marketing spikes typically last.
- Session affinity: if you pin sessions to workers, we size for memory per-session; if ephemeral, we optimize for throughput. For KV-backed sessions we generally recommend ephemeral session spawn + prefix caching to maximize utilization.

Operational suggestions:
- Enable adaptive batching with a low-latency window (~30–40ms) for conversational flows; it buys throughput without hurting p95 if you tune queue depth.
- If you want consistent p95 < 200ms for long responses, we may need to bias towards lower batch sizes and more reserved nodes.

I'll put a draft SKU map together once you provide the regional split and confirm model family. Jordan — happy to take the worksheet once Elena returns it and produce the cost envelope + fallback routing suggestions.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Infra Solutions, Redwood Inference

(Inline note) attachment: none

From: Elena Park <elena@novacorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@novacorp.com, ops-eng@novacorp.com
Date: Fri, 06 Jun 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — preliminary traffic snapshot

Thanks Jordan & Marissa — attached is the worksheet with regional split and a short answers tab. A few answers inline:

- Regional split: ~85% US, ~10% EU, ~5% APAC (initial pilot US-only).
- Model family: start with a quantized 13B for cost reasons; evaluate a 70B variant for advanced assistants in Q1.
- Burst duration: marketing blasts typically ~3–8 minutes peak, sometimes a 20–30 minute plateau if campaign gains traction.
- Sessions: agent workload uses ephemeral sessions with a pinned KV store per user (we can change if needed).

Also attaching a small contract outline (novacorp_contract_outline.pdf) that legal asked to see early — it lists our data-retention needs and a few telemetry requirements. We'll need to confirm Redwood's default retention windows for logs and audit traces.

Links: sample telemetry on Drive (https://drive.google.com/novacorp/traffic-snapshot) and a DocuSign link for preliminary NDAs (https://www.docusign.com/novacorp/precommit).

Please confirm when you have the SKU map and an initial cost range so I can bring it to procurement next week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Elena

Attachments: novacorp_contract_outline.pdf (PDF, 24KB), novacorp_telemetry_sample.csv (CSV, 28KB)
